# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Canva, 17 November 2026

**Scope:** Developments from the search results, dated 2 to 10 November 2026. Each fact is cited to its source.

## Summary

Canva has restructured. On 3 November it announced cuts affecting 22% of its global workforce, about 1,271 staff, as it flattens its org chart and consolidates teams. The same week it expanded its OpenAI partnership and faced reports of further cuts or a hiring freeze.

## What changed

**Restructuring and layoffs**
- Canva lays off 22% of staff, about 1,271 people, to flatten the org chart and consolidate teams (https://www.computerworld.com/article/3816579/tech-layoffs-this-year-a-timeline.html).
- CEO Melanie Perkins said "small changes won't be enough" and that Canva needs to "re-found" itself around "small, empowered teams" (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304).
- The company is merging its product, growth and platform teams and reducing "subspecialisation," so remaining staff may take on broader responsibilities (https://tech.yahoo.com/general/breaking-news/article/tech-layoffs-tracker-2026-all-the-job-losses-across-canva-squarespace-amazon-microsoft-apple-meta-and-others-141507340.html).
- Departing staff get at least six months' salary plus other support (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304). Benefits include keeping their company MacBooks, a free year of LinkedIn Premium and career coaching (https://m.economictimes.com/news/international/world-news/canva-layoffs-2026-meet-ceo-melanie-perkins-who-plans-to-give-away-80-of-her-billion-dollar-fortune-as-1271-jobs-are-cut/articleshow/135575689.cms). Those leaving can also apply for US$10,000 grants to start a business or community project (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-04/canva-restructure-job-losses/107344304).
- Capital Brief reported previously unreported finance-division cuts in January, with 32 roles made redundant (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- Capital Brief also reported that Canva could announce another round of redundancies or a hiring freeze in November. Canva has not confirmed either (https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137).

**AI and partnerships**
- Canva expanded its OpenAI deal, gaining broader access to OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 models. The two companies will work on making them more economical to run, though no savings or costs were disclosed. This came days after Canva launched its second in-house AI model (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).
- OpenAI already powers Canva Code, which builds interactive designs, websites and apps from text descriptions (https://www.startupdaily.net/topic/business/canva-doubles-downw-with-openai-just-days-after-launching-its-2nd-in-house-ai-model).

**Marketing**
- Canva unveiled a campaign by new agency GS&P, "What Will You Canva Today?", with three comedy TV spots. The first aired during NBC Sunday Night Football on 1 November. Out-of-home and social work are also part of it (https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/419113/canva-unveils-campaign-by-new-agency-gsp.html).

**Hires and deals**
- No new hires or executive appointments were found in the results.
- The only acquisition-related data is an undated company profile listing deals from February to April 2026, including Ortto, SimTheory and Doohly (US$30M). These fall outside the 30-day window (https://tavily.com/knowledge/company/wafeqPWRLzYp).

## Source gaps
- No hiring or leadership-change news was found for the period.
- The company profile is undated, so its deal list cannot be confirmed as current.

## Open questions
1. After the 3 November restructure, is a further redundancy round or hiring freeze planned for November, and which teams would it affect?
2. How will the expanded OpenAI partnership and the second in-house model change Canva's product roadmap and partner priorities, and do you expect cost savings from running the models more efficiently?
3. With product, growth and platform teams merged, who will be our day-to-day counterparts and final decision-makers, and will "re-founding" Canva change our account or partner arrangements?
